notes: Passages are book/chapter/verse references; scripture text is intentionally not duplicated. Guided plans include original short study notes; the full-Bible schedule contains reading assignments only. Completion and reminders should be stored separately from this catalog. Chapter-only references imply the whole chapter; endChapter is inclusive; startVerse/endVerse, when present, are inclusive.

plans.title: New to the Bible
plans.description: A seven-day introduction to the Bible’s unfolding story, from creation to Jesus and the gospel.

days.title: The Beginning
days.introduction: God creates a good world and gives human beings responsibility within it.
reflectionQuestions: What do these chapters reveal about the Creator and human purpose?
days.takeaway: Our story begins with God's creation and care.

days.title: What Went Wrong?
days.introduction: Human disobedience brings shame and alienation, while God still seeks the people he made.
reflectionQuestions: What changes after Adam and Eve disobey God?
days.takeaway: Sin harms relationships, but God does not abandon his creation.

days.title: God Calls Abraham
days.introduction: God calls Abram to trust a promise whose fulfillment he cannot yet see.
reflectionQuestions: What does Abram's response teach about faith?
days.takeaway: Faith responds to God's promises with trust.

days.title: God Delivers His People
days.introduction: God hears Israel's suffering and acts to deliver them from Egypt.
reflectionQuestions: How does God reveal his character through these events?
days.takeaway: The God of Scripture hears and rescues.

days.title: Jesus Comes
days.introduction: The Gospels introduce Jesus as both born into human history and the eternal Word made flesh.
reflectionQuestions: What do these passages claim about Jesus?
days.takeaway: Jesus stands at the center of the Bible's message.

days.title: The Good News
days.introduction: Jesus announces God's kingdom; his death and the empty tomb are central to the gospel story.
reflectionQuestions: How are repentance, the cross, and resurrection connected?
days.takeaway: The gospel calls for a response to Jesus.

days.title: Responding to God
days.introduction: Jesus speaks of new birth, and Paul explains salvation by grace through faith.
reflectionQuestions: How do these texts describe God's gift and our response?
days.takeaway: Salvation is God's gift, received through faith.

plans.title: Who Is Jesus?
plans.description: Fourteen readings exploring Jesus’ identity, ministry, death, and resurrection.

days.title: The Word Made Flesh
days.introduction: John identifies Jesus as the eternal Word who entered human life.
reflectionQuestions: What does John say about Jesus before his earthly birth?
days.takeaway: Jesus is more than a remarkable teacher.

days.title: The Promised Messiah
days.introduction: In Nazareth, Jesus reads Isaiah and announces its fulfillment.
reflectionQuestions: What kind of mission does Jesus describe?
days.takeaway: Jesus understands his work in light of God's promises.

days.title: The Son of God
days.introduction: Jesus' baptism and early ministry introduce his identity and authority.
reflectionQuestions: What do people encounter when Jesus begins to teach?
days.takeaway: Jesus' authority is integral to his identity.

days.title: The One Who Calls
days.introduction: Jesus invites ordinary people and welcomes those others reject.
reflectionQuestions: Who does Jesus call, and what does following him require?
days.takeaway: Jesus calls people to follow him.

days.title: The Teacher
days.introduction: Jesus describes the character and witness of those in God's kingdom.
reflectionQuestions: Which teaching challenges your assumptions most?
days.takeaway: Jesus teaches a different way of life.

days.title: The Healer
days.introduction: Jesus heals a paralyzed man and claims authority to forgive sins.
reflectionQuestions: Why do the religious teachers object?
days.takeaway: Jesus addresses both visible suffering and the deeper problem of sin.

days.title: Lord of the Storm
days.introduction: Jesus calms the storm and leaves the disciples asking who he is.
reflectionQuestions: Why are the disciples astonished?
days.takeaway: Jesus displays authority over creation.

days.title: Friend of Sinners
days.introduction: Jesus seeks Zacchaeus, whose response reveals a changed life.
reflectionQuestions: How does Zacchaeus respond to Jesus' welcome?
days.takeaway: Jesus came to seek and save the lost.

days.title: The Good Shepherd
days.introduction: Jesus compares his care for his people to a shepherd who lays down his life.
reflectionQuestions: What distinguishes the good shepherd from a hired hand?
days.takeaway: Jesus knows and sacrificially cares for his people.

days.title: The Bread of Life
days.introduction: Jesus points beyond material bread to the life he gives.
reflectionQuestions: What kind of hunger is Jesus addressing?
days.takeaway: Jesus offers more than temporary satisfaction.

days.title: The Resurrection and the Life
days.introduction: At Lazarus's tomb, Jesus declares his power over death.
reflectionQuestions: What does Jesus ask Martha to believe?
days.takeaway: Jesus calls for faith in him even amid grief.

days.title: The Servant King
days.introduction: Jesus washes his disciples' feet and models humble service.
reflectionQuestions: How does Jesus redefine greatness?
days.takeaway: Following Jesus includes serving others.

days.title: The Crucified Savior
days.introduction: Jesus is crucified, forgives his enemies, and entrusts himself to the Father.
reflectionQuestions: What stands out about Jesus' words from the cross?
days.takeaway: The cross reveals both suffering and mercy.

days.title: The Risen Lord
days.introduction: Jesus' followers encounter the news of his resurrection and receive their commission.
reflectionQuestions: How does the resurrection change the disciples' understanding?
days.takeaway: The risen Jesus sends his witnesses into the world.

plans.title: Learning to Pray
plans.description: Seven days learning from Jesus and the Scriptures about sincere prayer.

days.title: Teach Us to Pray
days.introduction: Jesus responds when a disciple asks him to teach them to pray.
reflectionQuestions: What priorities appear in Jesus' model prayer?
days.takeaway: Prayer can be learned from Jesus.

days.title: Pray in Secret
days.introduction: Jesus warns against performing prayer for public approval or relying on many words.
reflectionQuestions: What motivates sincere prayer?
days.takeaway: Prayer is directed to God, not an audience.

days.title: The Lord's Prayer
days.introduction: Jesus' model includes worship, daily dependence, forgiveness, and protection.
reflectionQuestions: Which request do you tend to overlook?
days.takeaway: Prayer aligns our desires with God's purposes.

days.title: Ask, Seek, Knock
days.introduction: Jesus encourages persistent requests grounded in the Father's goodness.
reflectionQuestions: How does Jesus describe the Father's response?
days.takeaway: We can bring our needs to a good Father.

days.title: Honest Prayer
days.introduction: David moves from lament and questions toward trust.
reflectionQuestions: What does this psalm allow you to say to God?
days.takeaway: Honest sorrow has a place in prayer.

days.title: Pray with Thanksgiving
days.introduction: Paul links prayer and thanksgiving with the peace of God.
reflectionQuestions: What worries could you bring to God today?
days.takeaway: Prayer and gratitude belong together.

days.title: Keep Praying
days.introduction: The apostles call believers to persistent prayer in ordinary life and hardship.
reflectionQuestions: When do these passages encourage prayer?
days.takeaway: Prayer belongs throughout the Christian life.

plans.title: Finding Peace in God
plans.description: Seven passages about trusting God during fear, uncertainty, and hardship.

days.title: When Fear Rises
days.introduction: The psalmist admits fear while deliberately putting his trust in God.
reflectionQuestions: What does trusting God look like when you are afraid?
days.takeaway: Faith can be expressed in the midst of fear.

days.title: The Lord Is My Shepherd
days.introduction: David describes God's guidance and presence even in dark valleys.
reflectionQuestions: Which image of God's care speaks most to you?
days.takeaway: God's presence gives comfort in difficulty.

days.title: Bring Your Worries
days.introduction: Jesus tells disciples to seek God's kingdom instead of being ruled by anxiety.
reflectionQuestions: What examples does Jesus use to explain God's care?
days.takeaway: Jesus invites us to trust the Father's care.

days.title: Peace in Prayer
days.introduction: Paul teaches believers to turn anxious concerns into prayer with thanksgiving.
reflectionQuestions: How can thanksgiving reshape your response to worry?
days.takeaway: Bring your concerns to God in prayer.

days.title: Peace from Jesus
days.introduction: Before his departure, Jesus promises peace unlike the world's.
reflectionQuestions: What is the source of the peace Jesus offers?
days.takeaway: Jesus offers peace amid uncertainty.

days.title: God Is Our Refuge
days.introduction: Amid threats and upheaval, the psalm declares God a present refuge.
reflectionQuestions: What does the psalm say remains secure?
days.takeaway: God is a refuge when circumstances shake.

days.title: Hope Beyond Trouble
days.introduction: Paul affirms that suffering cannot separate believers from God's love in Christ.
reflectionQuestions: Which hardship does Paul name, and what is his conclusion?
days.takeaway: God's love in Christ remains steadfast.

plans.title: Growing Your Faith
plans.description: Fourteen days on trust, obedience, spiritual growth, and perseverance.

days.title: Faith Begins with Trust
days.introduction: Hebrews introduces faith as confidence in what God has promised.
reflectionQuestions: What does this passage say about approaching God?
days.takeaway: Faith begins by trusting God's reality and promises.

days.title: Abraham Believes
days.introduction: Abram trusts God's promise despite his unanswered longing for a son.
reflectionQuestions: Why is Abram's faith significant?
days.takeaway: God calls people to trust his word.

days.title: Faith and Obedience
days.introduction: James argues that genuine faith is demonstrated in action.
reflectionQuestions: How does James distinguish living faith from empty claims?
days.takeaway: Living faith bears fruit in conduct.

days.title: Learning God's Word
days.introduction: The psalmist treasures and meditates on God's instruction.
reflectionQuestions: How can Scripture shape daily choices?
days.takeaway: God's Word forms the habits of faith.

days.title: Growing Through Trials
days.introduction: James explains how trials can produce steadfastness and mature faith.
reflectionQuestions: What is the difference between trials and temptation here?
days.takeaway: Perseverance can deepen faith.

days.title: Trust in Hard Decisions
days.introduction: Wisdom calls for trusting the Lord rather than relying solely on personal understanding.
reflectionQuestions: What does acknowledging God in your ways involve?
days.takeaway: Trust shapes how we make decisions.

days.title: Remain in Christ
days.introduction: Jesus pictures disciples as branches dependent on the vine.
reflectionQuestions: What does abiding in Christ produce?
days.takeaway: Spiritual growth depends on remaining in Jesus.

days.title: The Spirit's Fruit
days.introduction: Paul contrasts the works of the flesh with the fruit of the Spirit.
reflectionQuestions: Which fruit would you like to cultivate?
days.takeaway: The Spirit reshapes character.

days.title: Renew Your Mind
days.introduction: Paul connects worship with a transformed mind and humble service.
reflectionQuestions: How does a renewed mind affect your view of yourself?
days.takeaway: Faith changes both thinking and behavior.

days.title: Pray with Confidence
days.introduction: Jesus' priesthood gives believers confidence to seek God's mercy and grace.
reflectionQuestions: Why can believers approach God's throne boldly?
days.takeaway: Jesus makes access to God possible.

days.title: Love One Another
days.introduction: Paul describes love as essential even amid impressive gifts and abilities.
reflectionQuestions: Which description of love challenges you most?
days.takeaway: Love is central to spiritual maturity.

days.title: Be Quick to Listen
days.introduction: James calls believers to receive God's word and practice it.
reflectionQuestions: Where does James connect hearing with doing?
days.takeaway: Growing faith expresses itself in action.

days.title: Run with Endurance
days.introduction: The writer urges persistence by looking to Jesus.
reflectionQuestions: What helps believers endure hardship?
days.takeaway: Fixing our attention on Jesus sustains perseverance.

days.title: Keep Growing
days.introduction: Peter describes qualities believers should diligently cultivate.
reflectionQuestions: Which qualities build upon faith in this passage?
days.takeaway: Spiritual maturity calls for ongoing diligence.

plans.title: Understanding Salvation
plans.description: A seven-day exploration of the biblical message of sin, grace, Jesus, and faith.

days.title: The Good Creation
days.introduction: God makes human beings in his image and gives them a good place in creation.
reflectionQuestions: What was God's original design for people?
days.takeaway: Human life begins with God's good purpose.

days.title: The Problem of Sin
days.introduction: Genesis describes rebellion, and Paul explains humanity's need for God's righteousness.
reflectionQuestions: What does sin disrupt, and why do we need grace?
days.takeaway: Sin creates a need we cannot resolve by ourselves.

days.title: God's Love
days.introduction: Jesus explains God's love and the gift of eternal life through belief in the Son.
reflectionQuestions: How does this passage connect God's love and belief?
days.takeaway: God's saving initiative comes from love.

days.title: Christ Died for Us
days.introduction: Paul says Christ died for sinners and made reconciliation possible.
reflectionQuestions: What did Christ do while people were still sinners?
days.takeaway: Christ's death displays undeserved grace.

days.title: Jesus Rose Again
days.introduction: Paul identifies Christ's death and resurrection as essential to the gospel.
reflectionQuestions: Why is the resurrection indispensable to Christian hope?
days.takeaway: The resurrection is central to the gospel.

days.title: Saved by Grace
days.introduction: Paul says salvation is God's gift, not something earned by works.
reflectionQuestions: How are grace, faith, and good works related?
days.takeaway: We are saved by grace through faith for good works.

days.title: Responding in Faith
days.introduction: The apostles call people to believe in Christ, repent, and respond to the gospel.
reflectionQuestions: What responses do these passages describe?
days.takeaway: The gospel calls us to turn to God in faith.

plans.title: The Life of Joseph
plans.description: Ten days following Joseph through betrayal, suffering, wisdom, and reconciliation.

days.title: Joseph's Dreams
days.introduction: Joseph's dreams intensify tension within Jacob's family.
reflectionQuestions: How do favoritism and jealousy shape the story?
days.takeaway: Family conflict sets Joseph's story in motion.

days.title: Betrayed by Brothers
days.introduction: Joseph's brothers sell him, and Jacob believes he is dead.
reflectionQuestions: What choices make the brothers' wrongdoing worse?
days.takeaway: Human betrayal has far-reaching consequences.

days.title: Faithful in Egypt
days.introduction: Joseph resists temptation yet suffers a false accusation.
reflectionQuestions: How does Joseph respond when obedience becomes costly?
days.takeaway: Faithfulness is possible even in unjust circumstances.

days.title: God Gives Wisdom
days.introduction: Joseph interprets dreams in prison and asks to be remembered.
reflectionQuestions: Where do you see Joseph acknowledging God?
days.takeaway: Joseph points beyond himself to God.

days.title: From Prison to Palace
days.introduction: Joseph interprets Pharaoh's dreams and is entrusted with preparing for famine.
reflectionQuestions: How does Joseph use his new responsibility?
days.takeaway: Wisdom and preparation can serve others.

days.title: The Famine Comes
days.introduction: The famine brings Joseph's brothers to Egypt without their recognizing him.
reflectionQuestions: How has Joseph's situation changed since Genesis 37?
days.takeaway: The story turns toward a difficult reunion.

days.title: Conscience and Responsibility
days.introduction: Joseph tests his brothers, who begin to face the consequences of their actions.
reflectionQuestions: What signs of changed attitudes appear?
days.takeaway: Past wrongs must be faced honestly.

days.title: A Brother's Sacrifice
days.introduction: Judah offers himself in Benjamin's place.
reflectionQuestions: How does Judah's response contrast with Genesis 37?
days.takeaway: Self-sacrifice shows meaningful change.

days.title: Joseph Reveals Himself
days.introduction: Joseph tells his brothers who he is and speaks of God's preserving purpose.
reflectionQuestions: How does Joseph hold their actions and God's provision together?
days.takeaway: God can bring preservation through human evil without excusing it.

days.title: Forgiveness and Providence
days.introduction: After Jacob's death, Joseph assures his brothers of his care.
reflectionQuestions: What does Joseph mean by God's good purpose?
days.takeaway: Joseph chooses mercy over revenge.

plans.title: The Life of David
plans.description: Twenty-one days following David’s calling, victories, failures, repentance, and legacy.

days.title: An Unexpected King
days.introduction: Samuel anoints David while God challenges assumptions based on appearance.
reflectionQuestions: What does God emphasize when choosing a king?
days.takeaway: God sees beyond outward appearance.

days.title: Serving with Courage
days.introduction: David enters Saul's service as a musician and attendant.
reflectionQuestions: How does David serve before ruling?
days.takeaway: Faithfulness often begins in ordinary service.

days.title: David and Goliath
days.introduction: David faces Goliath with confidence that the battle belongs to the Lord.
reflectionQuestions: What grounds David's courage?
days.takeaway: Trust in God shapes courageous action.

days.title: A Loyal Friend
days.introduction: Jonathan loves David despite the threat David poses to his family's throne.
reflectionQuestions: How does Jonathan demonstrate loyalty?
days.takeaway: Friendship may require costly faithfulness.

days.title: Fleeing for His Life
days.introduction: David becomes a fugitive as Saul pursues him.
reflectionQuestions: What pressures might David have faced?
days.takeaway: Faith can be tested in uncertainty.

days.title: A Chance for Revenge
days.introduction: David spares Saul's life despite the opportunity to kill him.
reflectionQuestions: Why does David refuse retaliation?
days.takeaway: Restraint can be an act of reverence.

days.title: Another Test of Mercy
days.introduction: David again refuses to take Saul's life.
reflectionQuestions: What is consistent in David's reasoning?
days.takeaway: Godly restraint may require repeated choices.

days.title: Loss and Grief
days.introduction: David mourns Saul and Jonathan rather than celebrating Saul's death.
reflectionQuestions: What does David's lament reveal?
days.takeaway: Honor and grief are not weaknesses.

days.title: David Becomes King
days.introduction: The tribes acknowledge David as king, and Jerusalem becomes his capital.
reflectionQuestions: Whom does David credit for his kingdom?
days.takeaway: Leadership brings stewardship and responsibility.

days.title: Bringing the Ark
days.introduction: David brings the ark toward Jerusalem amid joy and a sobering reminder of God's holiness.
reflectionQuestions: How are celebration and reverence held together?
days.takeaway: Worship calls for joy and reverence.

days.title: God's Covenant Promise
days.introduction: God promises an enduring royal house, and David responds with prayer.
reflectionQuestions: How does David react to God's promise?
days.takeaway: God's promises invite humble gratitude.

days.title: Kindness to Mephibosheth
days.introduction: David keeps his pledge to Jonathan by showing kindness to his son.
reflectionQuestions: What does David's action reveal about covenant loyalty?
days.takeaway: Faithfulness includes keeping promises.

days.title: David's Sin
days.introduction: David abuses royal power in his actions toward Bathsheba and Uriah.
reflectionQuestions: What choices deepen David's wrongdoing?
days.takeaway: Even powerful leaders are accountable for sin.

days.title: Confronted by Nathan
days.introduction: Nathan confronts David, who acknowledges his sin and faces consequences.
reflectionQuestions: What changes when David is confronted?
days.takeaway: Repentance begins by acknowledging wrongdoing.

days.title: A Prayer of Repentance
days.introduction: David pleads for mercy and asks God for a clean heart.
reflectionQuestions: What is David seeking beyond outward forgiveness?
days.takeaway: True repentance seeks inward renewal.

days.title: Trouble at Home
days.introduction: Violence and failures of justice fracture David's family.
reflectionQuestions: How does the narrative portray the cost of inaction?
days.takeaway: Unaddressed evil causes deep harm.

days.title: Absalom's Rebellion
days.introduction: Absalom seizes support and forces David to flee Jerusalem.
reflectionQuestions: How does David respond to losing control?
days.takeaway: Leadership may involve humility in crisis.

days.title: Grief for Absalom
days.introduction: David mourns Absalom after the rebellion ends.
reflectionQuestions: What tensions does David face as father and king?
days.takeaway: Victory does not erase personal sorrow.

days.title: A Song of Deliverance
days.introduction: David praises God as his refuge and deliverer.
reflectionQuestions: What names and images does David use for God?
days.takeaway: Remembered deliverance gives rise to praise.

days.title: Preparing the Next Generation
days.introduction: David prepares materials and instructs Solomon concerning the temple.
reflectionQuestions: How does David help a future leader succeed?
days.takeaway: Faithful leadership prepares others to serve.

days.title: David's Final Charge
days.introduction: David instructs Solomon as his life and reign come to an end.
reflectionQuestions: What does David emphasize about walking in God's ways?
days.takeaway: A lasting legacy includes a call to faithfulness.

plans.title: Walking Through James
plans.description: Seven days through the letter of James and its practical teaching.

days.title: Trials and Wisdom
days.introduction: James urges perseverance in trials and invites believers to ask God for wisdom.
reflectionQuestions: What does James say trials can produce?
days.takeaway: Faith grows through perseverance and wisdom.

days.title: Hear and Do
days.introduction: James contrasts merely hearing God's word with acting on it.
reflectionQuestions: What does James say true religion includes?
days.takeaway: God's word calls for action.

days.title: Favoritism Forbidden
days.introduction: James condemns partiality toward the wealthy in the Christian assembly.
reflectionQuestions: How does favoritism contradict love of neighbor?
days.takeaway: Faith should reshape how we treat people.

days.title: Faith That Acts
days.introduction: James illustrates why faith without corresponding action is dead.
reflectionQuestions: What examples does James use to explain active faith?
days.takeaway: Genuine faith expresses itself in deeds.

days.title: The Power of Words
days.introduction: James warns that the tongue can cause great harm and contrasts two kinds of wisdom.
reflectionQuestions: How can words reveal the condition of the heart?
days.takeaway: Wise faith changes our speech.

days.title: Humility and Tomorrow
days.introduction: James confronts quarrels, pride, judgment, and presumption about the future.
reflectionQuestions: What does it mean to submit plans to God?
days.takeaway: Humility shapes relationships and plans.

days.title: Patience and Prayer
days.introduction: James calls for justice, patience, truthfulness, and prayer.
reflectionQuestions: Where do patience and prayer appear in daily faith?
days.takeaway: Steadfast faith prays and acts with integrity.

plans.title: The Book of Proverbs
plans.description: One chapter of Proverbs each day for thirty-one days.

days.title: The Call of Wisdom
days.introduction: Proverbs 1 presents wisdom for practical decisions and character, including choosing counsel over foolish enticement.
reflectionQuestions: Where do you see choosing counsel over foolish enticement in this chapter?
days.takeaway: Seek wisdom in ordinary choices.

days.title: Wisdom Worth Seeking
days.introduction: Proverbs 2 presents wisdom for practical decisions and character, including seeking wisdom as a treasure.
reflectionQuestions: Where do you see seeking wisdom as a treasure in this chapter?

plans.title: The Gospel of John
plans.description: One chapter per day through the Gospel of John.

days.title: The Word and the Witness
days.introduction: John introduces Jesus as the eternal Word and records the testimony about him.
reflectionQuestions: What do the opening verses claim about Jesus?
days.takeaway: Jesus brings life and light.

days.title: New Life and New Worship
days.introduction: Jesus transforms water to wine and clears the temple.
reflectionQuestions: What do these signs reveal about his mission?
days.takeaway: Jesus calls for a new understanding of worship.

days.title: Born from Above
days.introduction: Jesus teaches Nicodemus about new birth and God’s love.
reflectionQuestions: Why is new birth necessary?
days.takeaway: God gives life through belief in the Son.

days.title: Living Water
days.introduction: Jesus speaks with a Samaritan woman about true worship.
reflectionQuestions: How does Jesus cross social barriers?
days.takeaway: Jesus offers living water.

days.title: Life and Judgment
days.introduction: Jesus heals a man and speaks of the Son’s authority.
reflectionQuestions: How does Jesus explain his relationship with the Father?
days.takeaway: Jesus has authority to give life.

days.title: The Bread of Life
days.introduction: Jesus feeds a crowd and teaches about the bread from heaven.
reflectionQuestions: What does Jesus ask people to seek?
days.takeaway: Jesus gives enduring life.

days.title: Division over Jesus
days.introduction: Jesus teaches at the feast and people dispute his identity.
reflectionQuestions: Why do people draw different conclusions about Jesus?
days.takeaway: Jesus calls people to discern his teaching.

days.title: The Light of the World
days.introduction: Jesus exposes the dangers of unbelief and speaks of true freedom.
reflectionQuestions: What is the difference between slavery and freedom in this chapter?
days.takeaway: Jesus offers freedom through truth.

days.title: Seeing and Believing
days.introduction: Jesus heals a man born blind amid conflict about spiritual sight.
reflectionQuestions: Who recognizes Jesus more clearly by the end?
days.takeaway: Spiritual sight involves responding to Jesus.

days.title: The Good Shepherd
days.introduction: Jesus describes himself as the shepherd who knows his sheep.
reflectionQuestions: How do his sheep recognize him?
days.takeaway: Jesus cares for his people.

days.title: The Resurrection and the Life
days.introduction: Jesus raises Lazarus and reveals authority over death.
reflectionQuestions: How does Martha express her faith?
days.takeaway: Jesus is the resurrection and the life.

days.title: The Hour Draws Near
days.introduction: Mary anoints Jesus, who enters Jerusalem before his death.
reflectionQuestions: What responses to Jesus appear here?
days.takeaway: Jesus approaches the cross intentionally.

days.title: The Servant Lord
days.introduction: Jesus washes feet and prepares his disciples for betrayal.
reflectionQuestions: What does the foot washing teach?
days.takeaway: Love expresses itself in humble service.

days.title: The Way, Truth, and Life
days.introduction: Jesus comforts his disciples and promises the Helper.
reflectionQuestions: What does Jesus promise those who love him?
days.takeaway: Jesus is the way to the Father.

days.title: Abide in Me
days.introduction: Jesus teaches about the vine, love, and the world's opposition.
reflectionQuestions: What fruit comes from abiding in Jesus?
days.takeaway: Abiding in Christ sustains discipleship.

days.title: The Spirit and Sorrow
days.introduction: Jesus promises the Spirit and speaks of grief turning to joy.
reflectionQuestions: How does Jesus prepare his disciples for hardship?
days.takeaway: Jesus gives hope beyond sorrow.

days.title: Jesus Prays
days.introduction: Jesus prays for himself, his disciples, and future believers.
reflectionQuestions: What themes shape Jesus’ prayer?
days.takeaway: Jesus intercedes for his people.

days.title: The Arrest and Trial
days.introduction: Jesus is arrested, questioned, and brought before Pilate.
reflectionQuestions: How does Jesus respond to those in power?
days.takeaway: Jesus remains steadfast as he is rejected.

days.title: It Is Finished
days.introduction: Jesus is crucified, dies, and is buried.
reflectionQuestions: What details does John emphasize at the cross?
days.takeaway: Jesus completes the work set before him.

days.title: The Empty Tomb
days.introduction: Mary and the disciples encounter the risen Jesus.
reflectionQuestions: What changes when Jesus appears?
days.takeaway: The resurrection calls for faith.

days.title: Follow Me
days.introduction: Jesus restores Peter and addresses following him.
reflectionQuestions: What does Jesus ask of Peter?
days.takeaway: Love for Jesus leads to faithful service.

plans.title: The Bible in One Year
plans.description: Read every chapter of the 66-book Bible in 365 days, with Old Testament passages daily and New Testament passages on 260 days. Books follow their canonical order within each testament.

plans.title: The Power of Forgiveness
plans.description: Seven days exploring God's forgiveness, releasing resentment, and extending mercy to others.

days.title: A Heart That Needs Forgiveness
days.introduction: After his sin is exposed, David confesses his wrongdoing and asks God for mercy and a clean heart.
reflectionQuestions: What does David's prayer teach you about honest confession and repentance?
days.takeaway: Seeking forgiveness begins with acknowledging sin and turning to God.

days.title: God's Promise to Forgive
days.introduction: John teaches that walking in the light involves honesty about sin and trust in God's faithful forgiveness.
reflectionQuestions: Why is confessing sin different from pretending we have none?
days.takeaway: We can confess our sins knowing God is faithful and just to forgive.

days.title: The Father's Open Arms
days.introduction: In Jesus' parable, a younger son returns after squandering his inheritance, and his father welcomes him with compassion.
reflectionQuestions: What do the son's return and the father's response reveal about repentance and mercy?
days.takeaway: God's mercy is greater than the shame that can keep us from returning to him.

days.title: How Often Should We Forgive?
days.introduction: Jesus answers Peter's question about repeated forgiveness with a parable contrasting enormous mercy received and mercy withheld.
reflectionQuestions: How should remembering the mercy we have received affect the way we treat others?
days.takeaway: Those who receive mercy are called to extend mercy.

days.title: Letting Go of Bitterness
days.introduction: Paul urges believers to put away bitterness and anger and to practice kindness, patience, and forgiveness toward one another.
reflectionQuestions: Which attitude or action in these passages would help you respond differently to a hurt?
days.takeaway: Forgiveness is expressed through kindness, patience, and a willingness to release bitterness.

days.title: Forgiveness Instead of Revenge
days.introduction: Jesus prays for those crucifying him, while Paul teaches believers to refuse revenge and overcome evil with good.
reflectionQuestions: What is the difference between refusing revenge and pretending a wrong was acceptable?
days.takeaway: We can entrust justice to God rather than repay evil with evil.

days.title: Joseph's Example of Forgiveness
days.introduction: Joseph acknowledges the evil his brothers intended yet reassures them and provides for their families instead of seeking retaliation.
reflectionQuestions: How does Joseph acknowledge the wrong without letting it dictate his response?
days.takeaway: Forgiveness can acknowledge real harm while choosing mercy over revenge.

plans.title: Walking in Love
plans.description: Seven days learning to reflect God’s love in our words, relationships, and actions.

days.title: Love Begins with God
days.introduction: John teaches that love comes from God and is displayed in his sending of his Son.
reflectionQuestions: How does God’s initiative shape your understanding of love?
days.takeaway: We learn to love because God first loved us.

days.title: The Greatest Commandments
days.introduction: Jesus places love for God and love for neighbor at the heart of the commandments.
reflectionQuestions: How might love for God affect how you treat people this week?
days.takeaway: Love for God and neighbor belongs at the center of discipleship.

days.title: What Love Looks Like
days.introduction: Paul describes love through patient, generous actions rather than impressive words or gifts.
reflectionQuestions: Which characteristic of love is most challenging to practice?
days.takeaway: Love is shown through our choices and conduct.

days.title: Love Your Enemies
days.introduction: Jesus calls his disciples to love even those who oppose or mistreat them.
reflectionQuestions: What does Jesus ask his followers to do that goes beyond ordinary kindness?
days.takeaway: Christlike love is not limited to those who love us back.

days.title: Love in Action
days.introduction: John links the example of Christ’s sacrifice to practical care for people in need.
reflectionQuestions: What need could you respond to with practical help?
days.takeaway: Genuine love acts as well as speaks.

days.title: Love One Another
days.introduction: Jesus gives his disciples a command to love one another as he has loved them.
reflectionQuestions: How should others recognize Jesus’ disciples?
days.takeaway: Our love for one another points people toward Jesus.

days.title: Continue in Love
days.introduction: Jesus calls his disciples to abide in his love and bear fruit in loving obedience.
reflectionQuestions: What connection does Jesus make between his love and our actions?
days.takeaway: Lasting love grows from remaining close to Christ.

plans.title: Living with Joy
plans.description: Seven days discovering lasting joy in God through celebration, obedience, and hardship.

days.title: The Joy of Salvation
days.introduction: Jesus tells stories of a lost sheep and a lost coin to reveal joy when sinners repent.
reflectionQuestions: What do these parables teach about what brings joy in heaven?
days.takeaway: God rejoices when the lost are found.

days.title: Joy in God’s Presence
days.introduction: The psalmist finds hope and fullness of joy in the Lord’s presence.
reflectionQuestions: Where does the psalm locate lasting joy?
days.takeaway: Deep joy is grounded in fellowship with God.

days.title: Joy That Remains
days.introduction: Jesus connects abiding in his love and keeping his commandments with fullness of joy.
reflectionQuestions: How does Jesus describe the path to enduring joy?
days.takeaway: Joy grows as we remain in Christ’s love.

days.title: Joy in Hardship
days.introduction: James urges believers to count trials as joy because tested faith can produce steadfastness.
reflectionQuestions: How is joy during a trial different from enjoying the trial itself?
days.takeaway: Joy can rest in God’s work even when circumstances are painful.

days.title: The Joy of the Lord
days.introduction: After hearing God’s law, the people are encouraged to rejoice, share food, and draw strength from the Lord.
reflectionQuestions: Why does Nehemiah direct the people toward joy and generosity?
days.takeaway: God’s joy can strengthen his people.

days.title: Rejoice in the Lord
days.introduction: Paul calls believers to rejoice, pray with thanksgiving, and dwell on what is good.
reflectionQuestions: Which instruction could help redirect your thoughts today?
days.takeaway: Rejoicing in the Lord can accompany prayer and trust.

days.title: Joy No One Can Take
days.introduction: Jesus promises that the disciples’ sorrow will turn to joy after his departure and return.
reflectionQuestions: How does Jesus compare present sorrow with future joy?
days.takeaway: Christ gives hope that sorrow does not have the final word.

plans.title: Growing in Peace
plans.description: Seven days exploring peace with God, peace in the heart, and peace with others.

days.title: Peace with God
days.introduction: Paul says justification by faith brings peace with God through Jesus Christ.
reflectionQuestions: How is peace with God different from a calm day?
days.takeaway: Our deepest peace begins with reconciliation to God.

days.title: The Peace Jesus Gives
days.introduction: Jesus promises his disciples peace that is different from what the world gives.
reflectionQuestions: What makes Jesus’ peace distinct from temporary comfort?
days.takeaway: Christ’s peace can sustain us in uncertainty.

days.title: Trust Instead of Worry
days.introduction: Jesus points to the Father’s care while telling disciples not to be consumed by tomorrow’s worries.
reflectionQuestions: What examples does Jesus give of God’s provision?
days.takeaway: Peace grows as we seek God’s kingdom and trust his care.

days.title: Peace Through Prayer
days.introduction: Paul invites believers to bring concerns to God with thanksgiving and describes God’s guarding peace.
reflectionQuestions: What burden can you bring to God in prayer?
days.takeaway: Prayer opens our anxieties to God’s peace.

days.title: Pursue Peace with Others
days.introduction: Paul instructs believers to bless, refuse retaliation, and live peaceably as far as it depends on them.
reflectionQuestions: What is within your control when a relationship is strained?
days.takeaway: Peacemaking involves our choices, not control over others.

days.title: The Spirit and Peace
days.introduction: Paul contrasts works of the flesh with the fruit produced by the Spirit, including peace.
reflectionQuestions: What attitudes threaten peace in your relationships?
days.takeaway: Peace is part of the Spirit’s work in our character.

days.title: The God of Peace
days.introduction: Paul urges believers to forgive, love, and let Christ’s peace rule in their hearts.
reflectionQuestions: What practices help peace shape life in a community?
days.takeaway: Christ’s peace should guide how we live together.

plans.title: Practicing Long-Suffering
plans.description: Seven days learning biblical patience with people, trials, and God’s timing.

days.title: God Is Patient
days.introduction: God declares himself merciful, gracious, and longsuffering, while remaining just.
reflectionQuestions: How does God describe his patience alongside his other attributes?
days.takeaway: Patience reflects the character of a merciful and holy God.

days.title: The Lord Is Slow to Anger
days.introduction: The psalmist praises God’s compassion, mercy, and slowness to anger.
reflectionQuestions: How does remembering God’s compassion affect your response to others?
days.takeaway: We can practice patience because God has shown patience to us.

days.title: Patience with People
days.introduction: Paul calls believers to humility, gentleness, longsuffering, and bearing with one another in love.
reflectionQuestions: Where might patience protect unity in a relationship?
days.takeaway: Patience makes room for people to grow.

days.title: Slow to Speak and Anger
days.introduction: James urges believers to listen quickly, speak carefully, and be slow to wrath.
reflectionQuestions: Which part of James’ instruction is hardest when you are frustrated?
days.takeaway: Patient listening can prevent harmful reactions.

days.title: Wait for the Lord
days.introduction: David warns against fretting over evildoers and calls for trust and patient waiting.
reflectionQuestions: What does this psalm recommend instead of anger and fretting?
days.takeaway: Patience trusts God rather than rushing toward resentment.

days.title: The Farmer’s Patience
days.introduction: James uses the farmer and the prophets to encourage perseverance until the Lord’s coming.
reflectionQuestions: How does the farmer illustrate patient endurance?
days.takeaway: Longsuffering stays faithful when results take time.

days.title: Clothe Yourself in Patience
days.introduction: Paul tells God’s chosen people to practice patience, forbearance, and forgiveness.
reflectionQuestions: What would patient forgiveness look like in one relationship?
days.takeaway: Spirit-shaped patience shows itself in merciful relationships.

plans.title: Growing in Gentleness
plans.description: Seven days practicing God-shaped kindness, tenderheartedness, and gentle speech.

days.title: Kindness Reflects God
days.introduction: Paul contrasts humanity’s former way of life with the kindness and love of God our Savior.
reflectionQuestions: How did God show kindness toward people who had not earned it?
days.takeaway: Our kindness is rooted in God’s mercy.

days.title: A Gentle Answer
days.introduction: Proverbs contrasts a soft answer with harsh words that stir up anger.
reflectionQuestions: How could a gentler response change a difficult conversation?
days.takeaway: Gentle speech can turn conflict away from anger.

days.title: Jesus Welcomes the Vulnerable
days.introduction: Jesus welcomes children when his disciples try to send them away.
reflectionQuestions: What does Jesus’ response teach about making room for others?
days.takeaway: Gentleness treats people with dignity and care.

days.title: Be Kind to One Another
days.introduction: Paul tells believers to speak helpfully and to show kindness, tenderheartedness, and forgiveness.
reflectionQuestions: Do your words tend to build others up or wear them down?
days.takeaway: Kindness is expressed through speech and actions.

days.title: Gentle Restoration
days.introduction: Paul calls spiritual believers to restore someone caught in sin with a spirit of meekness and self-examination.
reflectionQuestions: Why does helping someone require humility and care?
days.takeaway: Correction should aim to restore rather than humiliate.

days.title: Kindness to the Overlooked
days.introduction: In the parable of the good Samaritan, a stranger gives practical help to a wounded man.
reflectionQuestions: What acts of mercy make the Samaritan a neighbor?
days.takeaway: Gentleness and kindness notice suffering and respond.

days.title: The Servant’s Manner
days.introduction: Paul instructs the Lord’s servant to avoid quarrels, teach patiently, and correct with gentleness.
reflectionQuestions: How can you defend truth without becoming argumentative?
days.takeaway: A gentle spirit can be firm without being harsh.

plans.title: Living in Goodness
plans.description: Seven days learning to reflect God’s goodness through integrity and good works.

days.title: What Is Good?
days.introduction: Micah summarizes what the Lord requires: justice, mercy, and humble walking with God.
reflectionQuestions: How does this passage define a life that pleases God?
days.takeaway: Goodness joins right conduct with humility and mercy.

days.title: God Is Good
days.introduction: David praises the Lord and invites others to experience his goodness and care.
reflectionQuestions: Where does David direct people to look for goodness?
days.takeaway: God’s goodness is the foundation for ours.

days.title: Let Your Light Shine
days.introduction: Jesus calls his followers salt and light so others may see their good works and glorify the Father.
reflectionQuestions: What good deed might point someone toward God rather than yourself?
days.takeaway: Goodness is visible in actions that honor God.

days.title: Do Good to All
days.introduction: Paul urges believers not to grow weary of doing good and to use opportunities to help others.
reflectionQuestions: What makes it difficult to keep doing good without immediate results?
days.takeaway: Goodness continues even when service feels tiring.

days.title: A Life Full of Good Works
days.introduction: Tabitha is remembered for the good works and charitable acts she did for others.
reflectionQuestions: What do the people’s responses reveal about Tabitha’s life?
days.takeaway: Consistent acts of care can bless an entire community.

days.title: Overcome Evil with Good
days.introduction: Paul describes sincere love and urges believers not to repay evil with evil.
reflectionQuestions: Where could you choose an honorable response instead of retaliation?
days.takeaway: Goodness answers evil without imitating it.

days.title: Ready for Every Good Work
days.introduction: Paul connects God’s saving mercy with believers’ responsibility to be ready for good works.
reflectionQuestions: Why must good works be understood as a response to grace?
days.takeaway: God’s grace leads us into lives of active goodness.

plans.title: Growing in Faith and Faithfulness
plans.description: Seven days exploring trust in God and a steady, faithful life.

days.title: Faith Begins with Trust
days.introduction: Hebrews describes faith as confidence in God and what he has promised.
reflectionQuestions: What does this passage say is necessary when approaching God?
days.takeaway: Faith starts with trusting God’s character and promises.

days.title: Faithful in Small Things
days.introduction: Jesus teaches that trustworthiness in small responsibilities matters.
reflectionQuestions: How do everyday decisions reveal whether you are faithful?
days.takeaway: Faithfulness is practiced in ordinary responsibilities.

days.title: God Is Faithful
days.introduction: Amid grief, the writer recalls God’s enduring mercies and great faithfulness.
reflectionQuestions: What truth helps the writer find hope amid suffering?
days.takeaway: God’s faithfulness gives us a reason to keep trusting.

days.title: Stewards Who Are Faithful
days.introduction: Paul says those entrusted with a stewardship should be found faithful, while final judgment belongs to the Lord.
reflectionQuestions: Whose approval matters most when you are entrusted with a task?
days.takeaway: Faithfulness means serving responsibly before God.

days.title: Faith That Acts
days.introduction: James shows that living faith becomes visible through action.
reflectionQuestions: How do the examples in this passage connect belief and obedience?
days.takeaway: Genuine faith expresses itself through faithful actions.

days.title: Holding Fast to Hope
days.introduction: Believers are encouraged to hold fast their confession because the One who promised is faithful.
reflectionQuestions: How does God’s faithfulness encourage your perseverance?
days.takeaway: We remain faithful by relying on the faithful God.

days.title: Faithful to the End
days.introduction: Near the end of his ministry, Paul looks back on having fought the good fight and kept the faith.
reflectionQuestions: What would it mean for you to finish your course faithfully?
days.takeaway: Faithfulness is a lifelong commitment, not a single moment.

plans.title: The Strength of Meekness
plans.description: Seven days learning humility, teachability, and strength under God’s direction.

days.title: Learn from Jesus
days.introduction: Jesus describes himself as meek and lowly in heart and invites the weary to find rest in him.
reflectionQuestions: How does Jesus’ character differ from worldly ideas of greatness?
days.takeaway: Meekness is strength expressed through humility and care.

days.title: The Meek Are Blessed
days.introduction: In the Beatitudes, Jesus calls the meek blessed and promises they will inherit the earth.
reflectionQuestions: What kind of character does Jesus honor in these blessings?
days.takeaway: God values humility rather than self-importance.

days.title: Moses and Meekness
days.introduction: When Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses, God defends his servant; the account describes Moses as very meek.
reflectionQuestions: How does Moses respond when Miriam faces judgment?
days.takeaway: Meekness does not require self-promotion or retaliation.

days.title: Receive the Word Humbly
days.introduction: James instructs believers to put away wickedness and receive the implanted word with meekness.
reflectionQuestions: What attitudes help you receive correction from Scripture?
days.takeaway: A meek heart remains teachable before God.

days.title: Restore with Meekness
days.introduction: Paul calls believers to restore the fallen gently while considering their own vulnerability.
reflectionQuestions: Why is self-examination important when correcting another person?
days.takeaway: Meekness offers help without superiority.

days.title: Answer with Gentleness
days.introduction: Peter tells believers to give a reason for their hope with meekness and fear, keeping a good conscience.
reflectionQuestions: How can you explain your faith with conviction and respect?
days.takeaway: Meekness can speak truth without aggression.

days.title: The Humility of Christ
days.introduction: Paul urges believers to put others first and points to Christ’s humility and obedience.
reflectionQuestions: Which attitude of Christ challenges your pride?
days.takeaway: Meekness grows as we follow Jesus’ humble example.

plans.title: Practicing Temperance
plans.description: Seven days learning Spirit-led self-control over desires, words, and actions.

days.title: The Spirit Produces Self-Control
days.introduction: Paul contrasts the desires of the flesh with the fruit of the Spirit, ending with temperance.
reflectionQuestions: What contrast do you see between impulses and life led by the Spirit?
days.takeaway: Self-control is a fruit of walking by the Spirit.

days.title: Guard Your Reactions
days.introduction: Proverbs places control over one’s spirit above strength in battle.
reflectionQuestions: Why might mastering your temper require greater strength than winning a fight?
days.takeaway: Controlling our reactions is a form of real strength.

days.title: A City Without Walls
days.introduction: Proverbs compares a person without self-control to a city without walls and warns against excess.
reflectionQuestions: How do these images illustrate the danger of unrestrained desires?
days.takeaway: Healthy limits protect our choices and character.

days.title: Run with Discipline
days.introduction: Paul compares the Christian life to athletes who train with restraint toward a lasting goal.
reflectionQuestions: What habits might need training rather than a quick decision?
days.takeaway: Self-control develops through purposeful discipline.

days.title: Watch Your Words
days.introduction: James explains the great power of the tongue and the damage uncontrolled speech can cause.
reflectionQuestions: When are your words hardest to restrain?
days.takeaway: Self-control includes careful, truthful speech.

days.title: Resist Temptation
days.introduction: Paul teaches that God is faithful amid temptation, while Jesus answers temptation with Scripture.
reflectionQuestions: How did Jesus respond to temptation, and what help does Paul promise?
days.takeaway: Temptation calls for vigilance, reliance on God, and wise action.

days.title: Train for Godliness
days.introduction: Peter urges believers to add temperance to knowledge as part of growing spiritual maturity.
reflectionQuestions: How does self-control fit among the qualities Peter calls believers to develop?
days.takeaway: Temperance belongs to a growing and fruitful Christian life.

plans.title: Overcoming Temptation
plans.description: Seven days learning to recognize temptation, resist deception, and rely on God when faced with difficult choices.

days.title: Understanding Temptation
days.introduction: James distinguishes testing, which can produce endurance, from temptation arising through sinful desire. God does not entice people to evil.
reflectionQuestions: How does James describe the progression from desire to sin?
days.takeaway: Recognize temptation early instead of allowing desire to take control.

days.title: The First Deception
days.introduction: The serpent questions God’s words, and Adam and Eve choose disobedience despite God’s command.
reflectionQuestions: How does the serpent distort what God said?
days.takeaway: Compare tempting claims with what God has actually said.

days.title: Jesus Resists Temptation
days.introduction: In the wilderness Jesus faces the tempter and answers each challenge with Scripture.
reflectionQuestions: What does Jesus’ response teach about knowing and applying God’s Word?
days.takeaway: Use Scripture to answer lies and choose obedience.

days.title: Watch and Pray
days.introduction: In Gethsemane Jesus urges the disciples to watch and pray even as they struggle to stay awake.
reflectionQuestions: Why is watchfulness necessary when our intentions are stronger than our resolve?
days.takeaway: Prayer and alertness help prepare us for moments of weakness.

days.title: God Provides a Way to Endure
days.introduction: Paul warns against overconfidence and reminds believers that God is faithful amid temptation.
reflectionQuestions: What does Paul warn against in verse 12, and promise in verse 13?
days.takeaway: Do not rely on confidence alone; look for the way to endure or escape temptation.

days.title: Flee and Pursue
days.introduction: Paul tells Timothy to flee youthful lusts and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace with others who call on the Lord.
reflectionQuestions: What can you actively pursue instead of simply trying not to sin?
days.takeaway: Replace harmful patterns with godly pursuits and supportive company.

days.title: Walk in the Spirit
days.introduction: Paul contrasts the works of the flesh with the fruit of the Spirit and calls believers to live by the Spirit.
reflectionQuestions: Which Spirit-produced quality could shape a temptation you face?
days.takeaway: Lasting resistance grows from a life directed by the Spirit.

plans.title: Dealing with Anger
plans.description: Seven days on understanding anger, responding wisely, avoiding destructive speech, and pursuing peace.

days.title: Slow to Anger
days.introduction: James urges believers to listen quickly, speak slowly, and be slow to wrath because human anger does not produce God’s righteousness.
reflectionQuestions: How might listening first change a recent disagreement?
days.takeaway: Make room to listen before reacting.

days.title: A Gentle Answer
days.introduction: Proverbs contrasts speech that calms conflict with harsh words that stir it up.
reflectionQuestions: What kind of words tend to escalate conflict, and what words might calm it?
days.takeaway: Choose words that reduce heat instead of adding to it.

days.title: Anger Without Sin
days.introduction: Paul acknowledges anger but forbids letting it lead to sin, bitterness, or harmful speech.
reflectionQuestions: What steps does Paul give for dealing with anger before it takes root?
days.takeaway: Address anger truthfully and promptly without using it to harm others.

days.title: What Comes from the Heart
days.introduction: Jesus teaches that harmful actions flow from the heart, not merely from external circumstances.
reflectionQuestions: What inner attitude might be influencing your response to a frustrating situation?
days.takeaway: Notice what your reactions reveal about the heart.

days.title: Restrain Your Words
days.introduction: Proverbs contrasts a fool who vents every feeling with the wisdom of restraint and warns about hasty speech.
reflectionQuestions: What could you do before speaking when you feel provoked?
days.takeaway: Restraint gives wisdom room to guide a response.

days.title: Leave Revenge to God
days.introduction: Paul calls believers to resist retaliation, seek peace when possible, and overcome evil with good.
reflectionQuestions: How is seeking peace different from pretending a wrong never happened?
days.takeaway: Refuse revenge and pursue what is good without excusing harm.

days.title: Put on Compassion
days.introduction: Paul calls believers to clothe themselves in compassion, humility, patience, forgiveness, and love.
reflectionQuestions: Which practice from this passage could change how you handle conflict this week?
days.takeaway: Cultivate habits of compassion that outlast a moment of anger.

plans.title: Learning to Trust God
plans.description: Seven days exploring God’s faithfulness, trusting him when the way is unclear, and responding with prayer and obedience.

days.title: Trust Beyond Understanding
days.introduction: Proverbs calls us to trust the Lord with all our heart and acknowledge him in our ways rather than treating our own understanding as final.
reflectionQuestions: Where do you find it hardest to trust God instead of your own judgment?
days.takeaway: Trust God while seeking to walk wisely in his ways.

days.title: God Keeps His Promises
days.introduction: Abram receives God’s promise in an uncertain situation and believes the Lord.
reflectionQuestions: What did Abram have to trust before he could see the outcome?
days.takeaway: God’s promises invite faith even when the outcome is not yet visible.

days.title: Trust in Fear
days.introduction: The psalmist acknowledges fear and repeatedly turns toward trust in God.
reflectionQuestions: How can the words “what time I am afraid” change how you think about faith?
days.takeaway: Trust does not require pretending fear is absent.

days.title: God Is Present in Trouble
days.introduction: The psalm describes God as refuge and strength amid upheaval, then calls his people to recognize his sovereignty.
reflectionQuestions: Which image from this psalm encourages you during uncertainty?
days.takeaway: God remains a refuge when circumstances are unstable.

days.title: Bring Every Concern to God
days.introduction: Paul urges believers to pray with thanksgiving and directs their thoughts toward what is true and worthy of praise.
reflectionQuestions: What concern could you bring honestly to God in prayer today?
days.takeaway: Trust expresses itself in prayer and thoughtful obedience.

days.title: Trust Jesus in the Storm
days.introduction: When a storm threatens the disciples, Jesus calms the wind and sea and challenges their fear.
reflectionQuestions: What do the disciples learn about Jesus from this event?
days.takeaway: Our confidence rests in who Jesus is, not in perfect circumstances.

days.title: Walk by Faith
days.introduction: Paul looks beyond present troubles toward the life God promises and says believers walk by faith, not by sight.
reflectionQuestions: How does future hope shape the choices Paul describes for the present?
days.takeaway: Keep living to please God even when you cannot see the whole path.

plans.title: Strengthening Your Marriage
plans.description: Seven days on covenant commitment, sacrificial love, wise communication, forgiveness, and serving one another in marriage.

days.title: God’s Design for Marriage
days.introduction: Genesis describes the first union of husband and wife, and Jesus affirms the seriousness of their one-flesh bond.
reflectionQuestions: What do companionship and commitment contribute to marriage?
days.takeaway: Treat marriage as a committed partnership worthy of care.

days.title: Love That Serves
days.introduction: Paul describes love as patient, kind, truthful, enduring, and free from selfishness; these qualities also matter in marriage.
reflectionQuestions: Which description of love most challenges how you treat your spouse?
days.takeaway: Express love through consistent actions, not merely feelings.

days.title: Mutual Care and Honor
days.introduction: Paul begins with mutual submission in reverence for Christ and calls spouses to sacrificial love and respect.
reflectionQuestions: What would sacrificial care and genuine respect look like in your daily routines?
days.takeaway: Seek your spouse’s good with love, dignity, and honor.

days.title: Listening Before Speaking
days.introduction: James emphasizes attentive listening and restraint, while Proverbs warns against answering before hearing.
reflectionQuestions: What could change if you listened to understand rather than to respond?
days.takeaway: Healthy communication begins with patient listening.

days.title: Forgiveness and Repair
days.introduction: Paul urges believers to bear with one another, forgive grievances, and put on love. Forgiveness does not remove the need for honesty, repentance, or rebuilding trust.
reflectionQuestions: Is there a hurt that needs a sincere conversation, accountability, or forgiveness?
days.takeaway: Practice mercy while taking responsibility for harm and rebuilding trust wisely.

days.title: Build Each Other Up
days.introduction: The apostles call believers to encourage and seek one another’s good, and Proverbs praises gracious words.
reflectionQuestions: How could you offer specific encouragement to your spouse this week?
days.takeaway: Use your words and actions to strengthen, not diminish, one another.

days.title: A Partnership That Prays
days.introduction: Ecclesiastes celebrates the practical strength of companionship, and Paul urges prayer and thanksgiving in every circumstance.
reflectionQuestions: What shared concern or gratitude could you bring to God together?
days.takeaway: Make space for partnership, gratitude, and prayer through life’s seasons.

plans.title: Parenting with Biblical Wisdom
plans.description: Seven days exploring how to guide children with love, wise instruction, patient discipline, and a faithful example.

days.title: Children Are a Gift
days.introduction: Scripture describes children as a gift, and Jesus welcomes them with personal attention and care.
reflectionQuestions: How might seeing children as people to cherish shape the way you parent today?
days.takeaway: Receive the responsibility of parenting with gratitude and care.

days.title: Teach Along the Way
days.introduction: Israelite parents are called to speak of God’s commands throughout ordinary daily life.
reflectionQuestions: What everyday moment could become an opportunity for a simple conversation about God?
days.takeaway: Faith is taught through consistent, everyday conversations.

days.title: Lead by Example
days.introduction: A parent’s actions can give weight to the values they teach; Paul also commends an example in conduct, love, faith, and purity.
reflectionQuestions: What behavior would you like your child to learn by watching you?
days.takeaway: Model the character you hope to nurture.

days.title: Correct with Care
days.introduction: Children are told to honor their parents, while parents are warned not to provoke or discourage them.
reflectionQuestions: How can you correct a child while protecting their dignity and encouraging growth?
days.takeaway: Discipline should instruct and guide, not crush or humiliate.

days.title: Listen Before You Speak
days.introduction: Scripture connects listening and gentle speech with wisdom, especially when emotions rise.
reflectionQuestions: How could you respond differently the next time your child is upset or makes a mistake?
days.takeaway: Patient listening can open the door to wise instruction.

days.title: Pray for Wisdom
days.introduction: Parents do not have every answer. James encourages asking God for wisdom, and Paul urges believers to bring concerns to God.
reflectionQuestions: What specific parenting decision or concern can you bring to God in prayer?
days.takeaway: Seek wisdom rather than relying only on your own instincts.

days.title: Entrust Their Growth to God
days.introduction: Scripture values teaching the young while reminding us that growth ultimately belongs to God; wisdom sayings are not guarantees about every child’s future.
reflectionQuestions: What faithful action is yours to take, and what outcome must you leave in God’s hands?
days.takeaway: Parent faithfully, remembering that you cannot control every outcome.

plans.title: Overcoming Worry and Anxiety
plans.description: Seven days of Scripture about bringing fears to God, receiving his care, and facing uncertain days with wisdom and support.

days.title: God Knows Your Needs
days.introduction: Jesus points to birds and flowers to teach his followers about the Father’s care and the limits of worrying about tomorrow.
reflectionQuestions: Which concern most often pulls your thoughts into tomorrow?
days.takeaway: Focus on today’s responsibilities while trusting God with tomorrow.

days.title: Bring Your Concerns to God
days.introduction: Paul invites believers to make their requests known to God with thanksgiving and directs their minds toward what is worthy.
reflectionQuestions: What worry could you put into words in an honest prayer today?
days.takeaway: Prayer is a place to bring anxiety, not a demand to pretend it is absent.

days.title: When Fear Is Real
days.introduction: The psalmist names his fear directly and chooses to turn toward God in the middle of danger.
reflectionQuestions: How does this psalm make room for both fear and faith?
days.takeaway: Feeling afraid does not prevent you from trusting God.

days.title: You Are Not Forgotten
days.introduction: Peter encourages humble reliance on God and says believers can cast their cares upon him because he cares for them.
reflectionQuestions: Which burden have you been trying to carry alone?
days.takeaway: God’s care invites you to bring him what weighs on you.

days.title: Strength for the Present
days.introduction: In a book shaped by suffering, the writer remembers God’s compassion and mercy amid grief.
reflectionQuestions: What does it mean to look for God’s mercy while circumstances remain difficult?
days.takeaway: Hope can coexist with sorrow and unanswered questions.

days.title: You Do Not Have to Carry It Alone
days.introduction: Scripture encourages mutual support as well as personal responsibility, reminding us that companionship matters during difficulty.
reflectionQuestions: Who is a trustworthy person you could ask to listen or help with a practical need?
days.takeaway: Seeking support can be an expression of wisdom and humility.

days.title: Rest in God’s Faithfulness
days.introduction: The psalm celebrates God’s watchful care, and Jesus comforts his disciples with the peace he gives.
reflectionQuestions: Which promise or truth from this week would you like to remember when anxiety returns?
days.takeaway: Return to God’s care one day at a time.

plans.title: Finding Your Purpose
plans.description: Seven days examining God’s creation, our calling in Christ, the gifts we receive, and faithful service in ordinary life.

days.title: Created with Meaning
days.introduction: Human beings bear God’s image and have been given dignity and responsibility within creation.
reflectionQuestions: How does being made in God’s image affect your understanding of your worth?
days.takeaway: Your value begins with the Creator, not with your achievements.

days.title: Created for Good Works
days.introduction: Paul teaches that salvation is God’s gift and that believers are created in Christ Jesus for good works.
reflectionQuestions: What good work is already in front of you today?
days.takeaway: Purpose includes responding to grace through faithful action.

days.title: Seek First God’s Kingdom
days.introduction: Jesus redirects his disciples from competing treasures and anxious striving toward the priorities of God’s kingdom.
reflectionQuestions: What priority competes most with seeking God’s kingdom?
days.takeaway: A meaningful life begins with rightly ordered priorities.

days.title: Use the Gifts You Have
days.introduction: Believers receive different gifts to use in serving others; no single gift defines a person’s worth.
reflectionQuestions: What ability or opportunity could you use to benefit someone else?
days.takeaway: Your gifts are opportunities for service.

days.title: Be Faithful in Ordinary Work
days.introduction: Paul calls believers to do their work sincerely as service rendered to the Lord.
reflectionQuestions: How might your attitude change if you viewed a routine responsibility as service to God?
days.takeaway: Ordinary tasks can be done with extraordinary faithfulness.

days.title: Love Your Neighbor
days.introduction: Jesus’ parable of the good Samaritan makes neighbor-love practical and costly rather than merely theoretical.
reflectionQuestions: Who near you has a need you can respond to this week?
days.takeaway: Purpose is often revealed through loving the person in front of you.

days.title: Walk Humbly and Faithfully
days.introduction: Micah emphasizes justice, mercy, and humility, while Paul prays for love and discernment as believers grow.
reflectionQuestions: What simple, faithful next step can you take without knowing every detail of the future?
days.takeaway: You can live with purpose without seeing the whole path ahead.

plans.title: The Power of Prayer
plans.description: Seven days exploring prayer through Scripture: access to God, confession, intercession, persistence, and dependence on his will.

days.title: Come Boldly to God
days.introduction: Because Jesus is our great high priest, believers are invited to approach God’s throne for mercy and help.
reflectionQuestions: What does this passage say makes it possible to approach God with confidence?
days.takeaway: Prayer begins with the access Jesus provides.

days.title: Pray According to God’s Will
days.introduction: John connects confidence in prayer with God’s will, and Jesus models honest requests joined to surrender in Gethsemane.
reflectionQuestions: How can you pray honestly about what you want while remaining open to God’s will?
days.takeaway: Confident prayer is not the same as controlling the outcome.

days.title: Confession and Renewal
days.introduction: David celebrates the relief of acknowledged sin, while John calls believers to walk in the light and confess their sins.
reflectionQuestions: Is there anything you need to bring into the light before God?
days.takeaway: Confession is a response to God’s mercy and truth.

days.title: Intercede for Others
days.introduction: Paul urges prayers for all people, including leaders, and asks believers to pray for his own ministry.
reflectionQuestions: Whom could you pray for specifically today, beyond your immediate needs?
days.takeaway: Prayer expands our concern beyond ourselves.

days.title: Keep Asking and Seeking
days.introduction: Jesus tells the parable of the persistent widow to encourage his disciples to pray and not lose heart.
reflectionQuestions: What is the difference between persistent prayer and demanding your own timetable?
days.takeaway: Persistence in prayer expresses ongoing dependence on God.

days.title: Prayer in the Church
days.introduction: As Peter is imprisoned, the church prays earnestly for him; the account shows a community bringing urgent needs before God.
reflectionQuestions: How could you participate more intentionally in praying with or for other believers?
days.takeaway: Prayer is part of the shared life of the church.

days.title: Pray and Live Faithfully
days.introduction: James calls for prayer in suffering and sickness, while Paul commends ongoing prayer and thanksgiving.
reflectionQuestions: What simple practice would help prayer become a regular part of your life?
days.takeaway: Keep praying through every season, trusting God’s faithfulness.

plans.title: The Power of the Word
plans.description: Seven days discovering the truth, power, and reliability of God’s Word—and learning to see yourself and your circumstances through what Scripture actually promises.

days.title: God Cannot Lie
days.introduction: God’s promises are dependable because his character is truthful and unchanging. Hebrews points believers to the certainty of God’s promise and oath as an anchor of hope.
reflectionQuestions: How does knowing that God cannot lie change the way you respond to his promises?
days.takeaway: God’s trustworthy character gives us a sure foundation for hope.

days.title: The Word That Creates and Accomplishes
days.introduction: God speaks and creation responds. Isaiah compares his word to rain that accomplishes his purposes. Scripture shows the authority and effectiveness of God’s word without suggesting that God could speak falsely.
reflectionQuestions: What do creation and Isaiah’s promise reveal about the power and purpose of God’s word?
days.takeaway: What God speaks is powerful and accomplishes his purposes.

days.title: Written for Our Instruction
days.introduction: People can be mistaken or unreliable, but Scripture equips believers with truth, correction, and instruction. Instead of letting every outside voice define reality, we can test what we hear against God’s word.
reflectionQuestions: Which voices most shape how you think, and how can Scripture help you evaluate their claims?
days.takeaway: Let God’s truth guide what you believe and how you live.

days.title: Who Does God Say You Are?
days.introduction: Those who receive Christ are described as God’s children. Believers are also called to live as his people, showing his praises. These truths give an identity rooted in grace rather than the labels others assign.
reflectionQuestions: Which description of believers in these passages most challenges the way you see yourself?
days.takeaway: In Christ, your identity rests on God’s grace, not other people’s judgments.

days.title: Redeemed and Made Right with God
days.introduction: Our standing before God is not earned by self-improvement. Through Christ, believers receive redemption and are made right with God by faith. Grace also calls us into a changed life.
reflectionQuestions: How is being made right with God through Christ different from trying to prove your own worth?
days.takeaway: Righteousness and redemption are gifts of God’s grace in Christ.

days.title: More Than Conquerors in Christ
days.introduction: Jesus has authority even over the storm, and Paul describes strength to endure both need and abundance through Christ. Romans assures believers that hardship cannot separate them from God’s love; it does not promise a trouble-free life.
reflectionQuestions: When circumstances feel overwhelming, what do these passages actually promise you about Christ’s presence and love?
days.takeaway: Hardship is real, but Christ sustains his people and God’s love remains secure.

days.title: Whose Report Will You Believe?
days.introduction: Scripture calls God’s word a sword and describes it as living and discerning. Knowing its truth matters, but so does receiving it humbly and putting it into practice. The question is not whether our words can control circumstances, but whether we will trust and obey God’s word.
reflectionQuestions: What is one false label, fearful assumption, or unhelpful belief you can bring under the light of Scripture—and what action will follow?
days.takeaway: Believe God’s word, learn it carefully, and live by its truth.
